# Jubilees Chapter 33 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Reuben's sin with Bilhah; sexual law codes

---

**33:1** And Jacob went to the land of the south and dwelt at the tower of the flock between Ephrath and Bethlehem.

**33:2** And Rachel died there and was buried in the land of Ephrath, which is Bethlehem. And Jacob set up a pillar upon the grave of Rachel, on the road above her grave. It is the pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.

**33:3** And in those days Reuben lay with Bilhah the concubine of his father, and Jacob heard and was angry; and he was very grieved.

**33:4** And Jacob reproached Reuben, and he repented and confessed it, and Jacob forgave him. But Jacob did not go in to Bilhah after this.

**33:5** For he counted the defilement exceedingly great, because he had lain in the concubine's bed of his father. And he separated himself from her.

**33:6** And because of this the children of Israel are commanded not to defile themselves with their father's wife, and are not to uncover the skirt of their father.

**33:7** For this is unclean: a man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness, and such a man shall be put to death.

**33:8** And concerning a man who lies with his daughter-in-law, it is equally written and ordained: they shall be burned with fire, both of them.

**33:9** And concerning all the fornications and impurities and every unlawful union — it is written and ordained in the heavenly tablets.

**33:10** After Rachel's death, Jacob took Leah and moved with her to his father Isaac. And Isaac was exceedingly glad to see Jacob and Leah and all of Jacob's sons.

**33:11** And Jacob went to Isaac his father at Mamre, which is Hebron, in the fourth year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

**33:12** And Isaac was old and exceedingly great in years, and his two eyes were dim and he could not see.

**33:13** And Jacob said to Isaac his father: "Let my father not be sorrowful, for I have returned to thee, and I have much cattle and sheep and flocks, and thy grandsons are grown."

**33:14** And Isaac prayed over Jacob and blessed him with joy. And Jacob was glad before his father all the days of his life.

**33:15** And in the first year of the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Leah died. And Jacob buried her in the double cave at Mamre with Abraham and Sarah and Isaac and Rebekah his mother, by night.

**33:16** And they mourned Leah greatly. And Jacob mourned her greatly, and her sons also wept for her.

**33:17** And the LORD comforted Jacob after the death of Leah.

---

*EMET notes: The Reuben-Bilhah episode (vv.3-5) is treated more leniently in Jubilees than in Genesis 49:4 (where Reuben loses his firstborn status). Here Jacob forgives Reuben but separates from Bilhah. The legal section (vv.6-9) turns the narrative into a foundation for incest prohibitions, citing the heavenly tablets. Rachel and Leah's deaths are also placed in this chapter.*
